**Spikes**

I left that Claude running in a space called `ctx-s5`, so your ctx board and the herdr app are already showing the same session.

**The lesson.** herdr-core starts its default core from any `hc` call and keeps that caller's environment for its whole life. A pool worker's test did exactly that, so the core you then "started" was really the worker's: it pointed Claude at the local pool, turned transcript saving off, and used the Max config dir. I replaced it with a core started from a clean login shell (zero agent variables) and saved the rule to memory: the operator's core starts clean, and every test or job that touches hc must isolate its state. I'll hold the runtime-driver job's tests to that when they land.

All five spikes are written up in `spikes/SPIKES.md` on branch `spikes-herdr`, to merge with phase 1. The three pool jobs (hub view model, collector hc support, runtime drivers) are still running.

earlier.assistant_text:
Yes: the install is portable, and I've done it for you.

**What the installers actually do.** Neither needs admin. They unpack into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\herdr-app` and `…\herdr-core`, add those folders to your user PATH, and drop a Start-menu shortcut. The archives are plain, so I downloaded both from WSL, verified the checksums in the release manifests, and unpacked them into those same folders. I did not touch PATH or the Start menu. Removing both folders undoes it.

- `C:\Users\RMellor\AppData\Local\Programs\herdr-app\herdr-app.exe` (0.1.13)
- `C:\Users\RMellor\AppData\Local\Programs\herdr-core\herdr-core.exe` (0.1.18, with its ConPTY dll). The app looks for the core in exactly that folder, so no PATH entry is needed.
- `C:\Users\RMellor\.config\herdr-app\` holds `ctx.json` (hub URL and token, host map) and a small `ctx-hello` mod for spike S4. The token is on NTFS, protected by your profile's ACL only, so this is spike-grade and the real install will handle it more carefully.

**One thing didn't work from here.** Starting the Windows core through WSL interop produced a running `herdr-core.exe` that never came up on its pipe, with an empty log. That may be the interop launch rather than a block, so please try it from a Windows terminal:

1. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\herdr-core\herdr-core.exe server start`, then `… server status`.
2. Run `herdr-app.exe`. If the sidebar shows "ctx board (spike) · hub ok · change N", S4 passes.
3. `herdr-core.exe machine add --name wsl --via "wsl.exe -e /home/dev/.local/bin/hc connect"`. In WSL first: `hc server start` (your own core; I removed the root-owned one).

If step 1 or 2 is refused, that's the endpoint-protection software blocking an unsigned exe (herdr says its Windows builds may be unsigned), and portability won't help. The fallback is the Linux herdr-app under WSLg, with nothing on the Windows side at all.

Separately, `sudo chown dev: ~/.local/bin/herdr-core ~/.local/bin/hc` in WSL when you get a moment.
